name: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation Associated with a Vascular Anomaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal consensus criteria; diagnosis based on clinical and laboratory findings

criteria.description: Confirmed presence of a vascular anomaly (e.g., venous malformation, arteriovenous malformation) by imaging or histopathology
Laboratory evidence of disseminated intravascular coagulation including thrombocytopenia, elevated D-dimers, prolonged PT and aPTT, and decreased fibrinogen
Clinical signs of bleeding or thrombosis consistent with DIC (e.g., petechiae, ecchymoses, mucosal bleeding)
Exclusion of other causes of DIC such as sepsis, malignancy, or trauma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a vascular anomaly plus laboratory evidence of DIC and clinical signs of bleeding or thrombosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, laboratory, and imaging findings; no standardized diagnostic scoring system exists specifically for this condition.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes petechiae, ecchymoses, and spontaneous bruising
searchTerms: frequent bleeding from skin and mucous membranes
repeated bleeding from mouth and skin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Visible vascular anomaly (e.g., venous malformation with swelling and discoloration)

searchTerms: bleeding lasts long after small cuts

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to anemia secondary to bleeding
searchTerms: weakness caused by low red blood cells

common.symptomName: Localized pain or swelling over vascular anomaly
searchTerms: pain or swelling over vascular lesion
localized discomfort near blood vessel anomaly

common.symptomName: Dyspnea due to pulmonary microthrombi or hemorrhage
searchTerms: shortness of breath from lung clots
breathing difficulty due to lung bleeding

occasional.symptomName: Neurological deficits secondary to cerebral microthrombi
searchTerms: brain function deficits from small clots
localized fluid buildup by vascular malformation

rare.symptomName: Acute limb ischemia due to thrombosis
searchTerms: sudden limb pain from blocked artery
acute loss of blood flow to limb

rare.symptomName: Severe disseminated microvascular thrombosis causing multi-organ failure
searchTerms: widespread small blood clots causing organ failure

laboratory: Prolonged prothrombin time (PT) and activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT)
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI demonstrating vascular anomaly (e.g., venous malformation, arteriovenous malformation)
CT angiography for detailed vascular mapping
Doppler studies showing altered blood flow in affected vessels
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; vascular anomalies may be sporadic or associated with somatic mutations in genes regulating angiogenesis
other: Histopathological confirmation of vascular anomaly if biopsy performed
Clinical correlation with bleeding and thrombosis symptoms

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of systemic infection or sepsis
Presence of blasts in peripheral blood or bone marrow

redFlags: Rapid onset of severe bleeding with hemodynamic instability
Signs of multi-organ failure due to microvascular thrombosis
Acute neurological deficits suggestive of cerebral thrombosis
references: Orphanet: Disseminated intravascular coagulation associated with vascular anomalies, ORPHA:717593
Levi M, et al. Disseminated intravascular coagulation: pathophysiology and clinical management. Blood Rev. 2020.
International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH) guidelines on DIC diagnosis and management
